clue.text: Wolves? You couldn't call them soccer players!

definitions.meaning: a group of wolves hunting together has a collective name

definitions.text: You couldn't call them soccer players!
definitions.meaning: the forwards in a rugby team share that collective name, so they play rugby, not soccer

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Wolverhampton Wanderers team are hopeless at football.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolverhampton Wanderers are nicknamed Wolves, a soccer team; the clue plays on the collective noun for wolves, which is also the name of rugby's forwards, not soccer players.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of wolves hunting together is called this, as is the set of forwards in a rugby team.

clue.text: After game see team somewhere by the water

parts.note: pool is the cue game played on a pocketed table
a side is a team in a match

explanation.surface: After the match, go and see the team relaxing by the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link word here, inviting you to look at the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The area beside a swimming pool is a location next to water.

clue.text: City types liable to lose their aspiration

definitions.meaning: traditional Londoners, born within the sound of Bow bells in the City of London
the classic East London accent drops the h-sound at the start of words, and an h-sound is called an aspirate

explanation.surface: Ambitious financiers in the City may give up their dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition, but in phonetics it is the breathy h-sound, which East End speech famously drops (''ello').
explanation.definitionFit: East Londoners from the old City district are the classic h-dropping speakers.

clue.text: I need franc changed — must be given new money

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone needing a franc converted must be supplied with fresh cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To refinance a debt or company is to fund it again with fresh capital.

clue.text: Vessel to be raised, having covered bottom of sea

indicators.note: the reversed words enclose the next piece
in a down clue, raised means the words to be are read upwards, backwards
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A ship is to be lifted after lying over the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TO BE into EBOT, which 'having covered' wraps round A, the last letter of 'sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: A German fast attack boat of the Second World War, a type of naval craft.

clue.text: Rebel in south, pressing

parts.note: a pressing matter is an urgent one

explanation.surface: A rebellion in the south is a pressing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel fighting against established authority, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Right away, obtains a bit of money, as one falling into line

indicators.note: with right away, that letter is removed from the verb

parts.note: to obtain something is to acquire it
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone who quickly gets a little cash is happy to conform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'immediately', but it tells you to drop R from ACQUIRES. 'as one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being acquiescent means agreeing quietly and conforming, which is what falling into line describes.

clue.text: Minister in Magic Circle?

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters of the next word are conjured into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman who belongs to the conjurors' famous society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a well-known British society of conjurors; 'Magic' is the anagram signal and 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a member of the clergy, a churchman.

clue.text: Advanced years of magistrate receiving cheers

indicators.note: the magistrate's title takes another piece inside it

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: An elderly magistrate is greeted with applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' is thanks here, not applause: TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age with weakening faculties is a time of life late in years.

clue.text: Cry making contact, having wasted time

indicators.note: wasting time here means losing the letter for time from the word

parts.note: touch is physical contact

explanation.surface: A shout of pain when two things touch, after time has been squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation of pain is a cry someone lets out when hurt.

clue.text: Following agreement, what Parisian will get involved?

indicators.note: the French word is drawn into the middle of the agreement

parts.note: consent is agreement
que is French for what

explanation.surface: After an accord is signed, what will a Parisian take part in?
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means resulting from or following on something.

clue.text: Tabloid's monetary fund is something astronomical

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a pot is a pool of money, a kitty

explanation.surface: A newspaper's prize fund is a vast sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astronomical' looks like 'huge sum', but is literal: a dark patch on the face of our star. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark cooler patch on the solar surface is an object studied in astronomy.

clue.text: Voyage here and there as green pirate at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A novice buccaneer roams about on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' is the anagram signal, fitting the pirate picture; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To peregrinate is to travel or wander from place to place, a verb for journeying about.

clue.text: Growing good fruit to begin with

indicators.note: the fruit comes first, ahead of the letter for good

parts.note: a raisin is a dried grape, a fruit

explanation.surface: Cultivating good fruit from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising crops or children means bringing them up, so the participle matches growing.

clue.text: Do they also have night vision?

definitions.text: Do they also have night vision?

parts.words: Do they also have night vision?
parts.note: people lost in reverie while awake have visions by daylight, so the joke asks whether they dream at night too

explanation.surface: A question about whether some people can see in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'night vision' sounds like seeing in the dark, but here means dreams while asleep, contrasting with the visions of those who drift off in waking hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle fantasists who drift into reverie while awake have visions in daylight.

clue.text: Chemical came with a diet specially formulated

indicators.note: formulated like a recipe, so the letters are mixed together anew

explanation.surface: A substance arrived along with a custom-designed eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetamide is an organic compound, the amide of acetic acid.

clue.text: Discharged, left place exempt from duties

parts.note: someone discharged is set free
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A released prisoner headed off to a tax haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour area where goods may be imported without customs charges.

clue.text: One could make hog speed? A different animal, more like!

definitions.text: One could make hog speed? A different animal, more like!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made different by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Could something make a pig run? More likely another beast would.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a farm dog might well make a hog hurry, and is a different animal from the hog.
explanation.definitionFit: A working farm dog herds livestock and could hurry a pig along.

clue.text: Visits planet and disappears

parts.note: visits as a verb: travels to a place
our own planet is the third from the sun

explanation.surface: Someone journeys to another world and vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from hunting: a fox going into its burrow hides from view.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to hide away, like a fox bolting into its den.

clue.text: Bill catches cat, one power-driven somehow

indicators.note: the bill's letters enclose the following pieces

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tom is a male cat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bill captures a cat, which somehow becomes motor-driven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not a name here but an account, abbreviated in the usual way; the power is nuclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven by nuclear power describes atomic engines, as in an atomic submarine.

clue.text: Dance suggested by Tintin?

parts.note: the boy reporter's name is read as tin plus tin, and each tin is a metal container also called a can, giving a dance name

explanation.surface: A dance inspired by the Belgian comic-strip reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintin is the Belgian cartoon hero; split, his name is two tins, and a tin is a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively high-kicking Parisian music-hall routine is a dance.

clue.text: Sinatra upset member of royal family once

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the singer's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra offends a former royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian empress or wife of the emperor belonged to the old imperial family.

clue.text: Drunk at this location offers defiant message

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
here means at this place

explanation.surface: A drunkard here sends a cheeky reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a sot. 'offers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a childish retort of triumph or defiance.

clue.text: Very good little son? Fancy that!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, little because shortened
well is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy that

explanation.surface: A doting parent amazed at how well-behaved their small boy is.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, swell describes something excellent, a dated slang word for great.

clue.text: Cinema she'd done up, given modern equipment maybe

indicators.note: done up means renovated, so the letters are refurbished into a new order

explanation.surface: The picture house she renovated was fitted with new kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mechanised means being equipped with machines, one kind of modern equipment.

clue.text: Female leading ancient church congregation

indicators.note: the female letter goes in front of the next piece

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: A woman at the head of an old congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of believers is a church body, from the sheep-pen image.

clue.text: Fish swirls by discharge

parts.note: a conge, from French conge, is a dismissal or discharge from service
reels as a verb means spins round, whirls

explanation.surface: Fish spin round near an outflow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' suggests outflow, but CONGE is a formal dismissal; 'by' is a link placing the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large marine creatures with long snake-like bodies, a kind of sea creature with fins.

clue.text: Label attached to the back of this animal

indicators.note: the label is joined after the preceding letter
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A tag fixed to the rear of a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult male deer is an animal.
